say: Bug report: it crashes in production.
Developer reply: 'works on my machine'. Classic. Ship the machine.
Dockerise the laptop! A tiny box with a tiny coffee stain.
The coffee stain is a required dependency.
Cache cleared. Still broken.
Now it is broken faster. Progress.
It is always DNS. If it is not DNS, it was DNS earlier.
Write that on a mug.
It is always the environment. Always. The environment is a very busy person.
It is also the cache, DNS, and the full moon.
Reproduce first. A radical, unfashionable idea.
Reproduction steps: step 1, 'it just happens'.
There are two hard problems: naming things, cache invalidation, and off-by-one errors.
I have a variable called 'data2'. It is not my best work.
data2 is a cry for help in four letters.
The next variable will be data2_final_REAL.
'x'. The universal name. Meaning to be found later.
Future you will be furious and will not even notice.
'doTheThing()'. Everyone loves it until the audit.
Auditors have no taste.
calculateTheTotalOfAllTheItemsInTheCartExcludingShippingAndTax. Poetry.
Fits exactly nothing on the screen.
Rubber duck advice: 'it is called user, not u'.
The duck does not judge. It also does not help.
Code review comment: 'nit: add a space.' Eleven times.
The real review was in the other tab: 'looks good to me'. In forty seconds. For 2,000 lines.
The tests are a single 'expect(true).toBe(true)'. We are fine.
Green checkmarks cure anxiety.
A kind review is rare. Like a bug-free Friday.
Add an emoji. The author will smile and merge.
'Why?' as the entire comment. Chaotic neutral.
The author is now a monk.
Strong stance. The author will reply 'fixed' and change nothing.
Then one nit again.
The bot says 'LGTM 🚀'. The bot has never read the code, and neither have we.
The pipeline is the real engineer.
Somebody wants to deploy at 4:55 on a Friday.
A brave soul. Or an enemy of weekends.
It works! The dashboard is green! Nothing is on fire!
...then Saturday morning. You know.
Monday: 'who deployed on Friday?' Silence. A cricket.
A beautiful office tradition.
Lunch is a time for the sacred sandwich, not for rollback.
Respect the sandwich.
Wise. Friday deploys are a haunted house with a pager.
Monday morning is a better ghost.
A feature flag: the polite way to say 'I am scared'.
Ship it dark and pray in the light.
Merge conflict. 47 files. Both of us changed the same line.
My version: tabs. Their version: spaces. The war is eternal.
Tabs: accessible, flexible, and somebody's strong opinion.
Spaces people have left the chat.
Auto-format on save. The only peace treaty ever signed.
Everyone is equally unhappy. A fair outcome.
Rewrite from scratch. Day one: confidence. Day thirty: the same line.
It is a circle.
Two spaces? Four? Eight for the brave? Every answer starts a feud.
The linter will pick for us. It always does.
Accept theirs, hope for the best, blame the merge tool.
The classic.
I explained my bug to a rubber duck and found it myself.
The duck did nothing. It just believed in me.

say: A duck for every desk. Name them by sprint.
HR will ask about the ducks.
Cats are worse listeners and better judges.
It stared at the screen. The bug fixed itself out of embarrassment.
A debugger! Very adult. Breakpoints and a feeling of control.
I give it two weeks before the prints return.
Logging is just prayer with timestamps.
The bug is in line 3. It always was.
print('here'), print('here 2'), print('why'). A classic trilogy.
Remove them before shipping. Or do not, and become a legend.
